fixes.explanation: That's right, friend. The text says it straight: "But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them." The commanders told him Ishmael had been sent to take his life, and Gedaliah didn't believe it. He didn't buy the warning.

That's the reason Nebuzaradan, Babylon's captain of the guard, gives. He says, "Because you people have sinned against the LORD and have not obeyed His voice, this thing has happened to you." He also says the LORD has done just as He said. The captain spells out the cause himself.

I get why you'd think so, since the man freeing Jeremiah is a Babylonian captain. But the text says the opposite. Nebuzaradan tells Jeremiah, "If it pleases you to come with me to Babylon, then come…" and then, "But if it seems wrong to you to come with me to Babylon, go no farther." It's an offer, and Jeremiah gets to choose.

Yes. Nebuzaradan says Gedaliah is the one "…whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah…" Gedaliah got his post from the king of Babylon. That's how Nebuzaradan describes it, right as he points Jeremiah toward Gedaliah.

That's right. Jeremiah went another way: "So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and stayed with him among the people who were left in the land." Babylon was on the table, and he went to Mizpah instead. I think that tells you plenty about where he wanted to be.

I see why you'd think so, since the warning came from Johanan and the commanders of the armies in the field. But the text says, "But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them." He heard that Ishmael had been sent to take his life, and he didn't buy it.

A bodyguard plan would be a lot gentler. But Johanan's offer is different: "Let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah…" He speaks privately to Gedaliah, and adds, "No one will know it." That's the offer on the table.
Taking Ishmael to Babylon isn't what Johanan says. He says, "Let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah…" and then adds, "No one will know it." It's a very serious offer, and he makes it privately.
